notes.title: CliRunner.invoke/isolation/Result flow in click.testing
answers: How does CliRunner isolate stdin/stdout/stderr and env?
How does CliRunner.invoke compute exit_code and exception?
What does capture='fd' do in CliRunner?
notes.body:
All in `src/click/testing.py`.
- `CliRunner.invoke`: optional `_FDCapture(1/2)` (capture="fd"; falls back to sys on OSError, ctor rejects fd on Windows) -> `with self.isolation(...)` -> `cli.main(args, prog_name, **extra)` -> build `Result`. String args use `shlex.split`.
- `CliRunner.isolation`: `StreamMixer` has stdout/stderr (`BytesIOCopy`, mirror writes to `output`) so `Result.output` is interleaved order. Wraps in `_NamedTextIOWrapper` (close is no-op). stdin via `make_input_stream`; `echo_stdin` uses `EchoingStdin` (+`_pause_echo` during prompts/getchar).
- Patches restored in `finally`: `termui.visible_prompt_func/hidden_prompt_func/_getchar`, `utils`/`_compat.should_strip_ansi`, `formatting.FORCED_WIDTH=80`, `pdb.Pdb.__init__`. Env: `make_env` merges runner and per-call env; `None` deletes key; restored via `old_env`.
- Exit handling in `invoke`: SystemExit -> exc_info always set, None code->0, `exception` only if nonzero, non-int code printed to stdout and exit_code=1. Other Exception: re-raised if catch_exceptions false (per-call overrides runner when not None), else exit_code=1. BaseException like KeyboardInterrupt is not caught.
- fd mode: captured bytes are written into the stdout/stderr buffers after the command, which mirrors into output.
- `Result`: stdout_bytes/stderr_bytes/output_bytes, return_value, exit_code, exception, exc_info, runner; text properties `stdout/stderr/output` decode with runner.charset, errors=replace, \r\n->\n.
